compare.label: How we compare
compare.heading: How our investment management compares.
compare.intro: Many advisors do some of these things well. Here's how our approach to managing your investments compares with a more traditional one.

rows.label: Where it starts
rows.us: What each dollar needs to do, when you'll need it, and how much risk makes sense for you.
rows.them: Often a risk questionnaire that points to a model portfolio.

rows.label: Planning
rows.us: Included in the advisory fee, and connected to how your money is invested.
rows.them: May be limited, billed separately, or handled apart from the investments.

rows.label: Taxes
rows.us: Which accounts hold which investments, and the tax cost of making changes, are part of each decision.
rows.them: Often handled separately from the investment decisions.

rows.label: Cash for spending
rows.us: A reserve sized to your needs, so a downturn is less likely to force you to sell investments at a bad time.
rows.them: Withdrawals often come from whatever the portfolio holds when you need cash.

rows.label: Investment approach
rows.us: Broad diversification and close attention to cost, instead of trying to predict what will lead next.
rows.them: May lean on market forecasts, or on a firm's own investment products.

rows.label: Accounts held elsewhere
rows.us: Your 401(k) and other accounts are part of the plan, even if they stay where they are.
rows.them: Advice may focus only on the accounts under management.

rows.label: Fees
rows.us: Published on this page, so you can see them before we ever meet.
rows.them: Not always published, which can make them hard to compare.

compare.footnote: “A traditional approach” describes common practices in our industry, not any particular firm. Every advisor works differently, so it's worth asking any advisor you're considering how they handle each of these.

otherCosts.heading: Other costs
otherCosts.body: Depending on how your portfolio is invested, there may also be third-party platform or investment expenses, which are separate from the One Life Advisory fee. We explain those before anything is implemented.

aum.label: Investment management
aum.heading: One fee for investment management and planning.
aum.intro:
For clients who have us manage their investments, our advisory fee is based on the amount we manage, and financial planning is included.

The fee is tiered, so each portion of the portfolio is charged at the rate for that tier.
aum.example: For example, if we manage $3 million, the first $1 million is charged at 0.80%, the next $1 million at 0.55%, and the third $1 million at 0.50%. The blended advisory fee would be approximately 0.62% per year.
details: The minimum annual advisory fee is $2,400.
Our minimum for investment management is $250,000 in assets available for us to manage.
In some cases, fees may be adjusted based on the size and complexity of the relationship.

included.label: What you get
included.heading: What the advisory fee covers.
included.intro: Here's what working with us can include for investment management clients. What we focus on depends on your situation.

items.name: Your Future Cash Flow
items.text: A year-by-year picture of the income your plan is designed to support, and where it may come from.

items.name: Income planning
items.text: Coordinating Social Security, pensions, and other income, including when each one starts, and what your portfolio needs to provide.

items.name: Withdrawal strategy
items.text: Which accounts to draw from, and when, planned year by year instead of by a fixed rule.

items.name: Reserves
items.text: Keeping the right amount available for emergencies and opportunities, so a surprise doesn't force you to sell investments at a bad time.

items.name: A portfolio with a purpose
items.text: Investments built around what each dollar needs to do, when you may need it, and how much risk makes sense for you.

items.name: Transition planning
items.text: Moving from what you own today to your new strategy, while managing any tax cost of the change.

items.name: Asset location
items.text: Choosing which accounts should hold which investments, with taxes in mind.

items.name: Ongoing management
items.text: Monitoring your portfolio and adjusting it as markets, tax rules, and your life change.

items.name: Tax bracket management
items.text: Planning each year across ordinary income, capital gains, Roth conversions, and the net investment income tax, with the goal of lowering your lifetime tax bill, not just this year's.

items.name: Easy-to-miss retirement taxes
items.text: Planning around required minimum distributions (RMDs), how Social Security is taxed, and income-based Medicare premiums (IRMAA).

items.name: Tax projections
items.text: Projecting your taxes years ahead, so you can spot opportunities while there's still time to act on them.

items.name: Charitable giving
items.text: Using gifting strategies like qualified charitable distributions and donor-advised funds when giving is part of your life. Support what you care about while reducing taxable income.

items.name: CPA coordination
items.text: Working from the same information as your CPA, so your planning and tax work stay on the same page. Your CPA remains responsible for preparing and filing your returns.

items.name: Coverage review
items.text: Reviewing the life, disability, and other insurance you already have, and where there may be gaps.

items.name: Long-term care planning
items.text: Deciding whether to insure it, set aside assets for it, or combine the two.

items.name: Healthcare before Medicare
items.text: Planning for coverage in the years before Medicare, and how your income choices can affect what you pay.

items.name: Insurance as an asset
items.text: Insurance is one of our specialties, and it's often overlooked in planning. We look at how life insurance cash value and annuities could support your income, taxes, or legacy, starting with what you already own and adding to it only when it makes sense.

items.name: Beneficiaries and account titling
items.text: Checking that who's listed, and how each account is owned, matches what you want.

items.name: Estate plan coordination
items.text: Reviewing how your accounts fit with your will, trusts, and other documents, alongside your attorney.

items.name: Giving while you're alive
items.text: Building in the support you want to give family or causes during your lifetime.

items.name: Regular reviews
items.text: A full review at least once a year, and help when decisions come up in between.

items.name: Plan updates
items.text: Revisiting your plan as life, markets, and tax law change.

items.name: Spending guidance
items.text: Knowing what your plan can support, so you can enjoy what you've built.

items.name: Professional coordination
items.text: Working alongside your CPA, attorney, and insurance professionals, and helping you find one if you need it.

planning.label: Planning only
planning.heading: Planning without investment management.
planning.intro: Our full relationship brings investment management and planning together, and it's how we prefer to work. If that isn't the right fit, we also offer planning on its own.

ongoing.name: Ongoing planning
ongoing.body: If you're below our minimum for investment management, we can work together through ongoing financial planning. We start by understanding your situation and building an initial written plan, then continue to review and update it as things change.
items: An ongoing annual fee of $3,600 to $15,000, billed monthly, based on the complexity of your situation and the scope of the work.

oneTime.name: One-time plan
oneTime.body: We learn your situation, build a written plan around what you want to accomplish, and walk through it with you. From there, you put it into action on your own.
items: A one-time fee of $3,600 to $15,000, based on the complexity of your situation and the scope of the work.
oneTime.note: A plan is a starting point. Life happens, tax rules change, and priorities shift, and the decisions that come up after the plan is written are often where an advisor matters most. That's why we prefer to work with clients on an ongoing basis.

planning.note: We agree on the fee with you before you decide to move forward.
